meta.scope: Yemen Batch 3 — Remittances, displacement, and agriculture densification under severe conflict constraints.

candidates.title: Remittance inflows statistics and framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from Cash Consortium and related sources
candidates.description: Statistics and framing of remittance inflows. Remittances have become the principal source of hard currency after the collapse of oil exports, estimated at over USD 7 billion in recent years and exceeding 30% of GDP. They are a critical household survival and external-financing mechanism.
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality external-financing node under current conditions. Replaces oil as the dominant hard-currency source.

candidates.title: Internal displacement statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix and OCHA sources
candidates.description: Statistics on internal displacement. Yemen hosts one of the world’s largest IDP populations; new displacement continues even in periods of relative de-escalation, with Ma’rib and other governorates as major destinations.

candidates.title: Agriculture production statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from national and USDA/FAO-aligned sources
candidates.description: Statistics on crop production. Sorghum, millet, wheat and other cereals are produced at low absolute levels relative to national food needs; Yemen is heavily import-dependent for staple cereals. Agriculture remains important for rural livelihoods under severe water and conflict constraints.
candidates.notes: Core primary-sector production node under import dependence and conflict stress.

candidates.title: Yemen remittances–displacement–agriculture densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from remittance, displacement and agricultural sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding remittance inflows, internal displacement statistics, and agriculture production into a coherent external-financing, humanitarian and primary-sector layer under severe conflict constraints.
